mainTopic: Once a father hands his daughter over to the husband's messengers, she leaves her father's authority for good. Even if she later goes back to his house, she does not return to her old status.
overview: The גמרא asks whether a girl whose father handed her to the husband's שלוחים goes back to her old status if she returns to her father's house. רבא answers from a ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל about the vows of an אלמנה and גרושה: once she leaves her father's רשות even for a moment, he can never cancel her vows again. רב פפא brings support from a משנה that a נערה המאורסה gets סקילה only while she is 'in her father's house'. רב נחמן בר יצחק brings another משנה: once she enters the husband's רשות for marriage, she counts as an אשת איש and the punishment is חנק. Then a new משנה begins. It rules that a father is not obligated to support his daughter, based on רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's teaching in the vineyard at יבנה. The גמרא infers that sons are an obligation and daughters a מצוה, then finds that this fits none of the three opinions in a ברייתא: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. It answers that the משנה can fit any of them. It begins with רבי מאיר, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe going back home restores her old status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that if the girl goes back to her father's house, she might return to her original status under his authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe when she goes back to her family's house, she goes back to her original situation?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that handing her to the husband's messengers makes her married. It asks whether returning to her father's home could undo that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule was that מסירה לשלוחי הבעל ends the father's רשות. The new question is whether this change is permanent or only lasts while she is on the way. If going home reverses it, the father would get his rights back.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (a suggestion that challenges what was just said)

phrases.english: But say: where she returns to her family's house
she returns to the original situation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier rule that מסירה לשלוחי הבעל makes her married, by asking whether that status can be reversed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The permanence of the status change caused by handing her to the husband's messengers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If her new status depends on her physically being in the husband's domain, then going back to her father's house should bring back her old status.

steps.title: רבא says this was already decided
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the school of רבי ישמעאל already settled this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: That question was already decided by the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his answer in short form: this was already decided. The גמרא is setting up the next move, where it quotes the source he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not answer from logic. He points to an earlier teaching. The rest of the passage will show how that ברייתא answers the question about returning home.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher of the school of רבי ישמעאל (a source of ברייתות)

phrases.english: Rava said: That was already decided by
the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָהוּא כְּבָר פַּסְקַהּ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by pointing to an existing source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to an earlier authoritative teaching (a ברייתא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going back to her father's house might restore her original status.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל shows that once she leaves her father's רשות, she does not return to it.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need to mention a widow's and a divorcée's vows?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק about the vows of an אלמנה and גרושה, and asks why it is needed, since such a woman is obviously under nobody's authority.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'But the vow of a widow or a divorcée, everything she has forbidden upon herself shall stand against her.' Why does the verse need to say this? Isn't she already outside both her father's authority and her husband's authority?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks why the Torah bothers to say that a widow's or a divorcée's vows stand. Obviously nobody can cancel them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal אלמנה or גרושה has already left her father's רשות and no longer has a husband. So nobody could cancel her vows anyway, and the פסוק seems unnecessary. This question sets up the ברייתא's answer, which reads the פסוק as teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the verse need to say this?
Is taken out of the category of

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"But the vow of a widow or a divorcée,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל אֲשֶׁר אָסְרָה עַל נַפְשָׁהּ יָקוּם עָלֶיהָ״,
phrases.english: everything she has forbidden upon herself shall stand against her"
Why does the verse need to say this?
Isn't she already out of her father's category
and out of her husband's category!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the ברייתא that רבא pointed to in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the פסוק about a widow's and a divorcée's vows comes to teach, since it seems obvious.

steps.title: Once she leaves her father's authority even briefly, he can never cancel her vows again
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that the פסוק is about a girl handed to the husband's messengers who was widowed or divorced on the way. Since she left her father's רשות for a moment, he can no longer cancel her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where the father handed her to the husband's messengers, or the father's messengers handed her to the husband's messengers, and she became widowed or divorced on the way. How would I think of her: as part of her father's house or her husband's house? So the verse tells you: once she has left her father's authority even for a moment, he can no longer cancel her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. The פסוק is about an unclear case, and it teaches that once she leaves her father's רשות, she never goes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The girl was handed over but never reached the חופה, so we might think she falls back under her father. The פסוק calls her vows binding, which means the father has lost his power to cancel them. This answers step 1: her status does not go back to what it was, even though she returns home.

keyTerms.meaning: The father handed her over to the husband's messengers

steps.whatToRemember: Once a girl leaves her father's רשות, even for a moment (by being handed to the husband's שלוחים), she never comes back under it. Returning to his house does not restore his rights.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the principle that leaving the father's רשות is permanent. It affects הפרת נדרים and the other rights that depend on her being under his authority.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, הֲרֵי שֶׁמָּסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: Rather, it is a case where the father handed her to the husband's messengers,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁמָּסְרוּ שְׁלוּחֵי הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: or the father's messengers handed her to the husband's messengers,
and she was widowed on the way or divorced,
how do I think of her:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית אָבִיהָ שֶׁל זוֹ, אוֹ בֵּית בַּעְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ?
phrases.english: is she in her father's house, or in her husband's house?
Rather, the verse comes to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצְאָה שָׁעָה אַחַת מֵרְשׁוּת הָאָב —
phrases.english: once she has left her father's authority for even a moment,
he can no longer cancel her vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הֲרֵי שֶׁמָּסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 3, and so completes רבא's answer to step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is about a girl widowed or divorced on the way to the husband's home. It teaches that leaving the father's רשות even briefly ends his power to cancel her vows for good.

steps.title: רב פפא brings support from the משנה about a betrothed girl
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says a משנה also teaches this. Someone who lives with a נערה המאורסה gets סקילה only if she is a נערה, a בתולה, מאורסה, and in her father's house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: We also learned this in a משנה: One who lives with a betrothed young girl is not liable unless she is a young girl, a virgin, betrothed, and in her father's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a second source to back up the idea that handing her over takes her out of her father's house. The גמרא is setting up the analysis of the משנה's wording in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four conditions for the special punishment of סקילה. The important one here is the last condition, 'in her father's house.' The next step will ask what that condition comes to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: We too have learned this in a Mishnah:
One who has relations with a betrothed young girl
is not liable unless she is
phrases.notes: Liable to stoning, the punishment for this specific case.

phrases.english: a young girl, a virgin, betrothed,
and she is in her father's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source from a משנה to support the principle about the father's רשות.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that handing her to the husband's messengers takes her out of her father's house.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about נערה המאורסה, which requires her to be 'in her father's house.'

steps.title: 'In her father's house' must exclude a girl handed to the husband's messengers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what each condition excludes and concludes that 'in her father's house' excludes a girl whose father handed her to the husband's messengers.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that 'young girl' excludes a grown woman, 'virgin' excludes a non-virgin, and 'betrothed' excludes a married woman. But what does 'in her father's house' exclude? Doesn't it exclude a case where the father handed her to the husband's messengers?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the משנה's conditions one by one. The last one, 'in her father's house,' must be excluding a girl who was handed over to the husband's messengers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the first three words clearly rules out some other kind of woman. 'In her father's house' needs its own purpose too. The best candidate is a girl already given to the husband's שלוחים, which would show she is treated as no longer in her father's house.

keyTerms.meaning: A grown woman (past the age of נערות)
A woman who is not a virgin
What does it come to exclude?

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא reads 'in her father's house' in the משנה as excluding a girl already handed to the husband's שלוחים. That supports treating her as out of her father's domain.
steps.confusionAlert: 'In her father's house' here does not just mean physically inside his home. It means still under his authority, before being handed to the husband's messengers.

phrases.english: It makes sense that "young girl" excludes a grown woman,
"virgin" excludes a non-virgin,
"betrothed" excludes a married woman.
"In her father's house": what does it come to exclude?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי מָסַר הָאָב לִשְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל?!
phrases.english: Doesn't it exclude where the father handed her to the husband's messengers?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the wording of the משנה quoted in step 5 to draw out רב פפא's proof.
steps.raayaObject: A girl handed to the husband's messengers is no longer considered 'in her father's house.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra condition 'בבית אביה' in the משנה, which must exclude something.

steps.title: Another proof from a משנה about a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes a משנה: once a woman has entered her husband's רשות for marriage, even before they have lived together, a man who lives with her gets חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: We also learned this in a משנה. If a man lives with a married woman, and she has already entered her husband's authority for marriage, even if she has not yet been with her husband, the man is punished with strangulation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings another משנה to support the idea from the earlier steps. He says entering the husband's רשות is enough to make a girl fully married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say 'once she entered the חופה'. It says 'once she entered the husband's רשות'. That wording sets up the inference in the next step: just entering his authority is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (in a משנה)
Full marriage, the second stage after אירוסין
Strangulation, the court's death penalty for adultery with a married woman

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
We, too, have learned this in a Mishnah:
One who lives with a married woman,
once she has entered the husband's authority for marriage,
even though she has not yet been with him,
the one who lives with her is punished by strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second supporting משנה, alongside רב פפא's proof in steps 5-6.
steps.raayaObject: A girl who has entered the husband's רשות (for example, by being handed to his messengers) counts as fully married.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סנהדרין about one who lives with an אשת איש.

steps.title: Merely entering his authority is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference from the משנה's wording: simply entering the husband's רשות is enough. The proof stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה speaks of her simply entering the husband's authority. Learn from it that this is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to the exact words of the משנה and concludes that the proof works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the משנה mentions only 'entering the husband's רשות' and no חופה, even a girl handed over to his messengers is included. So she already counts as a fully married woman: a man who lives with her gets חנק, not the סקילה of a נערה המאורסה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, a phrase that concludes a proof

steps.whatToRemember: A girl handed by her father to the husband's messengers has left her father's רשות. Her status as married begins then, even before the חופה.

phrases.english: She merely entered the husband's authority
phrases.notes: The משנה never mentions a חופה. Just being in his רשות is enough.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְנְסָה לִרְשׁוּת הַבַּעַל בְּעָלְמָא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the wording of the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Entering the husband's רשות, even by being handed to his messengers, is enough to count as נשואין.

steps.title: New משנה: a father need not support his daughter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a father is not obligated to support his daughter. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns this from the כתובה terms 'sons inherit, daughters are supported': both apply only after the father dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A father is not obligated to support his daughter. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה taught this before the חכמים in the vineyard in יבנה. The terms say 'the sons will inherit and the daughters will be supported.' Just as the sons inherit only after the father dies, so too the daughters are supported only after their father dies.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says a father has no legal duty to support his daughter while he is alive, and it gives רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules sit side by side in the כתובה terms, so he treats them the same way. Inheriting obviously happens only after death, so the daughters' support from the estate is also only after death. That means there is no legal duty during the father's lifetime.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'vineyard' in יבנה, where the חכמים gathered to learn

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say a father may not support his daughter, or that he shouldn't. It only says he is not legally obligated to.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A father is not obligated to support his daughter.
This teaching was expounded by
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
before the Sages in the vineyard in Yavne:
The sons will inherit, and the daughters will be supported.
phrases.notes: These are the standard terms of the כתובה. Sons inherit their mother's כתובה, and daughters get support from the father's estate.

phrases.english: Just as the sons do not inherit
except after the father's death,
so too the daughters are not supported
except after their father's death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאָב אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב בִּמְזוֹנוֹת בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה and a new topic: a father's duty to support his children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father has no legal obligation to support his daughter during his lifetime. Her right to support begins only after his death.

steps.title: Reading the משנה closely: son obligated, daughter a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers two things from the משנה's wording. A father is obligated to support his son. For his daughter there is no obligation, but there is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is his daughter's support that he is not obligated in, which implies that for his son's support he is obligated. And even for his daughter, there is no obligation, but there is a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה's exact words and pulls out what they imply. This is setting up the question in the next step about whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה singled out the daughter, which suggests the son is different and is obligated. It also said 'not obligated', not 'no מצוה', which suggests a מצוה still exists for the daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: But this implies, introducing an inference
A legal obligation that the court can enforce
A proper, good deed, but not enforced

phrases.english: Gemara:
It is for his daughter's support that he is not obligated,
but for his son's support, he is obligated.
His daughter too:
it is an obligation that there is not,
but a מצוה there is.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְזוֹנוֹת בִּתּוֹ הוּא דְּאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב, הָא בִּמְזוֹנוֹת בְּנוֹ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws implications from the wording of the משנה in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, supporting a son is an obligation, and supporting a daughter is a מצוה but not an obligation.

steps.title: Whose opinion fits this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows, and says it matches none of the three known opinions: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, or רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is our משנה? It is not רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה, and not רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem: the reading from step 10 does not seem to match any known תנא. The next step brings the source that shows why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 made the משנה a mix: an obligation for sons and a מצוה for daughters. The גמרא is about to show that each of the three תנאים holds something different.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is our Mishnah?
Not Rabbi Meir,
not Rabbi Yehuda,
and not Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, לָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading from step 10 by showing it fits no known תנא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה: an obligation for sons and a מצוה for daughters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should follow some known opinion, but this reading matches none of the three תנאים who rule on this question.

steps.title: The ברייתא with the three opinions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings three views. רבי מאיר says supporting daughters is a מצוה, and all the more so sons. רבי יהודה says supporting sons is a מצוה, and all the more so daughters. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says supporting daughters is an obligation only after the father dies, and during his life neither is supported.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: It is a מצוה to support the daughters, and all the more so the sons, who are busy with Torah. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: It is a מצוה to support the sons, and all the more so the daughters, because of the shame. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא says: It is an obligation to support the daughters after their father's death, but during their father's lifetime, neither sons nor daughters are supported.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that proves its claim in step 11, that our משנה matches none of these three תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה both treat sons and daughters alike as a מצוה, so neither says sons are an obligation. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא gives nothing at all during the father's lifetime, neither a son's obligation nor a daughter's מצוה. So none of them matches step 10's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so, an argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. Both say both children should be supported. They differ only on which child is the obvious case and which one is the 'all the more so'.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
It is a מצוה to support the daughters,
and all the more so the sons,
who are busy with Torah,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
It is a מצוה to support the sons,
and all the more so the daughters,
because of the shame.
phrases.notes: He means the shame a daughter would suffer if she had to go around begging.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says:
It is an obligation to support the daughters
after their father's death,
but during their father's lifetime,
both these and those are not supported.
phrases.notes: 'These and those' means both the sons and the daughters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind step 11's claim that no תנא fits the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה (son obligated, daughter a מצוה) matches none of the three תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא giving the views of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three views set out the full range of opinions on supporting children during the father's lifetime. The גמרא will need to fit the משנה somewhere in this range.

steps.title: The question again: the משנה fits none of the three opinions
steps.stepSummary: Now that the ברייתא has been quoted, the גמרא asks its question again and shows exactly where the משנה clashes with each opinion. רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה both hold that sons are only a מצוה. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא holds there is not even a מצוה for daughters while the father is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? If it is רבי מאיר, he said that supporting sons is only a מצוה! If it is רבי יהודה, he said that sons too are only a מצוה! If it is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא, according to him there is not even a מצוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its question, "Whose view is the משנה?", and now spells out why each of the three opinions in the ברייתא does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה's wording we learned that sons are an obligation and daughters are a מצוה (step 10). רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה make sons only a מצוה, which clashes with the first point. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא gives daughters nothing during the father's life, which clashes with the second point.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is [this person], but he said..., a way of showing a clash

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same question as step 11, asked again now that we know exactly what each תנא holds.

phrases.english: Whose view is our משנה?
If it is רבי מאיר,
but he said that sons are only a מצוה!
If it is רבי יהודה,
but he said that sons too are only a מצוה!
If it is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא,
then there is not even a מצוה!
phrases.notes: He means there is no מצוה to support a daughter while the father is alive, yet the משנה implies there is one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין? אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָא אָמַר בָּנִים מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 12 to the question from step 11, showing the clash with each opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two inferences drawn from the משנה in step 10: sons are an obligation, and daughters are a מצוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each of the three opinions contradicts at least one of these inferences, so the משנה seems to have no author.

steps.title: The answer: the משנה can fit any of the three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can be explained according to רבי מאיר, according to רבי יהודה, or according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא. Each explanation will be given in detail next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי מאיר; if you want, say it is רבי יהודה; if you want, say it is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an outline of its answer: any of the three תנאים could be the author. This line sets up the detailed explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not give up on the משנה. It will reread the משנה's words so that our inferences from step 10 no longer stand, and this can be done to fit each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: a way of offering one of several possible answers

phrases.english: If you want, say it is רבי מאיר;
if you want, say it is רבי יהודה;

phrases.aramaic: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא.
phrases.english: if you want, say it is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the קשיא of step 13 by listing three possible authors.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה so it fits each of the three opinions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה fits none of the three opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה can be read to fit any of them; the details come next.

steps.title: Reading the משנה like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי מאיר, the משנה means a father is not obligated to support his daughter, and the same is true for his son. There is a מצוה for the daughter, and by a קל וחומר also for sons. The גמרא then begins to explain why the משנה mentions only the daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say it is רבי מאיר, and this is what the משנה means: a father is not obligated to support his daughter, and the same is true for his son. But there is a מצוה for his daughter, and all the more so for sons. And the reason the משנה mentions only his daughter is to teach us this:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה according to רבי מאיר: sons are not an obligation either, so there is no clash with him. It ends by setting up its next point: why the משנה mentions only the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 we assumed that because the משנה said "daughter", sons must be different, meaning obligated. Here the גמרא says no: sons are the same, not obligated, and like daughters they are a מצוה, even more so. This removes the clash with רבי מאיר, but it leaves a question: why name only the daughter? The answer comes in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means: rereading the words
All the more so: if it is true in the weaker case, it is true in the stronger one
This is what it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: Here "the same is true for his son" means the son is also not obligated. It does not mean the son is supported by obligation.

phrases.english: If you want, say it is רבי מאיר,
and this is what it means:
A father is not obligated to support his daughter,
and the same is true for his son.
But there is a מצוה for his daughter,
and all the more so for sons.
And the reason it mentions only his daughter
is that it teaches us this:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְהָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the three detailed explanations promised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה: sons are the same as daughters, not different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning only the daughter implies that sons are obligated, which goes against רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sons are also not obligated, and both are a מצוה. Mentioning the daughter has another purpose, explained next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a careful inference from the משנה's wording, like the one in step 10, can be undone if the גמרא finds another reason for the wording.
